notes: Edit chosen for relation-property coverage (README, Shape per topic): `wholly_owned_subsidiary_of` carries `subproperty:subsidiary_of`, and `subsidiary_of` is transitive, so the edit gives a subproperty query and, through Audi's own parent, a transitivity query that discriminates (Rolls-Royce Motor Cars is not part of the Volkswagen Group before the edit, and is after). Derivability very_unlikely: the ownership is stated everywhere and follows from nothing. R1: the subject is Rolls-Royce Motor Cars Limited, the BMW company that has made Rolls-Royce cars since 2003, not Rolls-Royce Holdings (aero engines) and not the pre-2003 Rolls-Royce Motors, which Volkswagen owned from 1998 to 2003 and which became Bentley. That history makes the edit oddly plausible and is the main R1 risk for the original answers ('Is Rolls-Royce Motor Cars part of the Volkswagen Group?' is clearly no today); the prompts name Rolls-Royce Motor Cars and ask in the present tense. BMW licenses the Rolls-Royce name from Rolls-Royce Holdings, which does not change who owns the car company. Worlds: the V12 engines are stored by name as BMW engines (w1) or as engines from Rolls-Royce's parent (w2). w1 is consistent: an Audi-owned Rolls-Royce buying BMW engines is exactly what Rolls-Royce and Bentley did under Volkswagen from 1998 to 2003. w2 contradicts no firm fact outside the chain: nothing firm says Audi cannot build a V12. The Spectre is electric, so the engine prompts name the V12 models. Delete mirror of finance-replace-0013. The transitivity query has no counterpart here (BMW has no parent to pass through), so the second determinate query asks the parent's city, which is reachable only through the deleted link. In w1 the engines' maker survives by name, so the background queries split between BMW and does-not-know.
